items.title: Gender differences in the phonetic realization of the checked tone in Kaihui Xiang
items.authors: Yi Zhang(City University of Hong Kong); Aini Li(City University of Hong Kong)
items.abstract: Checked tones in Chinese languages often undergo smoothing, yet their phonetic mechanisms and sociophonetic conditioning remain understudied. This study examines the checked tone (T6) in Kaihui Xiang and tests whether gender differences indicate ongoing de-checking. Using F0, duration, and voice quality, we compare checked and unchecked tones across genders. Results show complete coda loss, but T6 remains distinct through a stable F0 contour and shorter duration. Phonation cues are also reorganized, with laryngealization shifting toward the syllable onset. Male speakers retain a conservative pattern with stronger durational truncation, while female speakers show weaker temporal cues and innovative phonatory dynamics. These patterns suggest Kaihui Xiang is in a late de-checking stage: tonal contrast is phonologized but phonetic grounding continues to shift, with gender asymmetry reflecting a gradual, socially conditioned redistribution of acoustic cues.

items.title: Age-dependent acoustic changes of the frication noise in dental sibilants produced by typically developing Polish children between 5 and 8 years of age
items.authors: Zuzanna Miodońska(Silesian University of Technology); Oliwia Skórzewska(Silesian University of Technology); Natalia Moćko(University of Silesia); Magdalena Krycha(University of Silesia); Michal Krecichwost(Silesian University of Technology)
items.abstract: The paper aims to investigate which acoustic properties of Polish dental fricatives /s, z/ are related to the age and sex of typically developing child speakers between 61 and 96 months of age. We analyzed speech samples collected from 88 children assessed as producing /s, z/ with a target (dental) place of articulation. The analysis comprises a set of typical spectral features and spectral features of the frication noise, which are treated as markers of sibilant articulation patterns. Linear mixed-effect models showed a significant age-related increase of fricative formant distance and spectral energy above 6 kHz for /s/ productions and a decrease in spectral energy below 2,5 kHz for /z/. The results present an age-dependent spectrum shift that may indicate improvement in articulatory precision. The results are a preliminary step in quantifying the acoustic patterns in the sibilant articulation development in typically developing children.

items.title: Age-related Differences in the Perception of Vowel Length Contrast in Northern Vietnamese: The Case of Hoang Van (Bac Ninh) Variety
items.authors: Van Dat Ta(Peking University); Baoya Chen(Peking University)
items.abstract: Vowel length contrasts in Northern Vietnamese are acoustically distinguished by both duration and spectral cues. This study investigated the perception of long and short vowels in this language and possible differences between older and younger listeners. The results show that, at the group level, listeners in both age groups relied primarily on vowel duration, with F1 and F2 serving as secondary cues. At the individual level, a small subset of older listeners relied mainly on F1. Furthermore, acoustically incongruent stimuli (e.g., long-vowel duration integrated with short-vowel quality) elicited significantly longer response times than congruent stimuli, without significant age-related differences. These findings indicate that both duration and spectral cues contribute to the perception of vowel length in Northern Vietnamese, and the reliance on F1 as the primary cue by some older listeners may indicate a possible ongoing sound change.

items.title: Age-related Differences in Acoustic Realization of Aspirated Fricatives in Shaxi Bai
items.authors: Xiaofang Zhang(University of Macau); Infat Lo(University of Macau); Yao Lu(Peking University)
items.abstract: Aspirated fricatives are realized through multiple interacting acoustic parameters rather than a single defining parameter. This study investigates the realization of aspirated fricatives in Shaxi Bai, focusing on three acoustic parameters: initial duration ratio, spectral center of gravity, and H1*–H2*. Acoustic data from 30 speakers across three age groups were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Results show that the relative magnitude of acoustic effects varies across fricative types and age groups. Temporal and spectral measures exhibit robust acoustic differences, whereas phonatory measure shows weaker and less consistent effects. Young speakers show a different covariation pattern among acoustic parameters, consistent with an ongoing reorganization of the aspiration contrast. These findings support a multidimensional account of aspirated fricatives and demonstrate intergenerational change in the relative contribution of temporal, spectral, and phonatory dimensions.

items.title: Listeners' gendered experiences and beliefs affect iconic pitch associations
items.authors: Sasha Calhoun(Victoria University of Wellington); Paul Warren(Victoria University of Wellington); Sara Gilbert(Victoria University of Wellington)
items.abstract: Certain intonational meanings have long been claimed to be iconic. For example, high vs. low voice pitch is physically linked to small vs. large body size, leading to affective meanings like submissiveness vs. dominance. While such associations have a physical basis, we claim they are also socially constructed, affected by language- and individual-specific ideological links, e.g. between dominance and masculinity. We present an experiment pairing a priming task and an Implicit Association Task (IAT) to probe variation in the strength of the pitch~size association. Primes were either strengthening or inhibiting and highlighted the affective link between size and submissiveness/dominance. The priming affected the strength of the pitch~size association as expected; however, the size of the effect differed by the gender of the listener and voice. These findings contribute to our understanding of how iconic meanings develop in speech and the crucial role of social experience and beliefs.

items.title: Age-Related Changes in Mandarin Lexical Tone Production: Acoustic Properties and Tonal Distinctiveness
items.authors: Zhongxuan Mao(Nanjing University of Science and Technology); Yan Feng(Nanjing University of Science and Technology); Chenyu Li(Johns Hopkins University)
items.abstract: Despite growing interest in age-related speech changes, how aging affects the production of lexical tones remains underexplored. This study compared the acoustic properties and the tonal distinctiveness between younger and older speakers. Seventy-eight native Mandarin speakers produced 236 syllables covering all four lexical tones. The results revealed that older speakers exhibited gender-divergent F0 centralization of different tones, contour flattening, greater F0 variability, and longer duration, with these age-related effects varying across tones and genders. Both Bhattacharyya distance and support vector machine classification accuracy showed decreased tonal distinctiveness of the tone system with age. Critically, classification confusion was concentrated on bidirectional T2↔T3 misclassifications. These production patterns paralleled previously reported perceptual difficulties in older adults, supporting the auditory-motor integration model.
